standard.title: Express and respond to opinions
standard.description: use interaction skills when engaging with topics, actively listening to others, receiving instructions and extending own ideas, speaking appropriately, expressing and responding to opinions, making statements, and giving instructions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students use interaction skills including turn-taking, active listening and responding to others' contributions (AC9E1LY02). They have not yet expressed and responded to opinions using specific sentence frames, or given instructions to others.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can use interaction skills to actively listen, express and respond to opinions, extend their own ideas, and give instructions in discussions.

nodes.label: Active listening and responding
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can demonstrate active listening by paraphrasing or responding to a partner's contribution before extending the discussion.
nodes.minimum_width: Paraphrase or summarise a partner's contribution before adding their own idea in a think-pair-share activity.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate active listening behaviours — eye contact, paraphrasing, responding to what was said — across different discussion contexts including class discussion, partner talk and small group work.
wider: Use sentence starters that acknowledge the speaker before responding: 'I agree that ... and I'd add ...', 'I heard you say ... and I think ...'
Identify when a response in a discussion did not acknowledge the previous speaker and discuss the effect on the conversation

response_modes.reason: Active listening in practice — actually paraphrasing before responding, not just nodding — requires repeated rehearsal across many discussion contexts. The skill does not vary meaningfully across topics; what varies is whether students habitually deploy it. Practice, not more types of listening, is the productive investment.

success_criteria: Student demonstrates at least one active listening behaviour (paraphrasing, acknowledgement) before adding their own contribution.
Student's response is connected to what the previous speaker said.

nodes.label: Expressing and responding to opinions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can express an opinion using appropriate language and respond to another's opinion — agreeing, disagreeing or offering an alternative — respectfully.
nodes.minimum_width: Express an opinion on a topic using a sentence starter, and respond to a classmate's opinion with at least one appropriate response frame.
nodes.typical_width: Express opinions using varied sentence starters across multiple discussion contexts; respond to others using frames that agree, disagree or offer an alternative; understand how to disagree respectfully.
wider: Compare how the same opinion sounds with a confident vs tentative sentence starter and discuss when each is appropriate
Practise a discussion where the task requires each participant to disagree respectfully with the previous speaker

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a range of sentence starters and response frames — agreeing, disagreeing, offering alternatives, extending. No single frame covers all interaction contexts. Building a usable repertoire across multiple discussion tasks is the productive investment.

success_criteria: Student expresses an opinion using an appropriate sentence frame.
Student responds to another's opinion in a way that acknowledges it and either agrees, disagrees or offers an alternative.

nodes.label: Giving and receiving instructions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can give clear instructions and receive instructions, asking clarifying questions where needed.
nodes.minimum_width: Give a set of at least two instructions for a familiar task in an appropriate sequence.
nodes.typical_width: Give and receive instructions across different contexts — classroom tasks, game rules, procedures — using appropriate sequencing language and checking for understanding.
wider: Compare instructions given verbally vs in written procedure form and discuss what each mode does well
Give instructions to a partner who must follow them without additional help, then evaluate clarity and completeness together
success_criteria: Student gives instructions in an appropriate sequence that a listener could follow.
Student can receive instructions and ask a clarifying question if something is unclear.
